title: Consolidate the budget and bring the deficit back to the 3% Maastricht limit
description: The ÖVP–SPÖ–NEOS government programme 'Jetzt das Richtige tun. Für Österreich.' (2025–2029) committed the coalition to restoring public finances after deficits of over 4% of GDP. Once the EU opened an excessive deficit procedure against Austria in July 2025, the government set the goal of reducing the general-government deficit to 3% of GDP by 2028 and leaving the procedure.
reasoning: Two double budgets (2025/2026 and 2027/2028) with consolidation measures have been adopted, and the deficit fell from 4.6% of GDP in 2024 to 4.1% in 2025 according to Statistics Austria. The EU deficit procedure could not be avoided, however, and the Finance Ministry still forecast 4.1% for 2026 and raised its 2027 forecast to 3.6% in October 2026, so the 3% target for 2028 remains to be met.
key_evidence: 18 June 2025: ÖVP, SPÖ and NEOS adopted the 2025 and 2026 budgets, each with a deficit of more than €18 billion; EU finance ministers opened the excessive deficit procedure on 8 July 2025 (Parliament, PK0696/2025)

Consolidation measures in the 2025 and 2027–2028 budget laws (BGBl. I Nr. 7/2025, Nr. 25/2025, Nr. 62/2026) include the end of the Klimabonus, a higher bank levy, a parcel tax, higher corporate tax on profits over €1 million and the non-indexation of family benefits
Statistics Austria: general-government deficit 4.6% of GDP in 2024 and 4.1% (€21.4 billion) in 2025
July 2026: Parliament adopted the 2027/2028 double budget with federal deficits of €15.5 billion and €13.2 billion, aiming at 3% in 2028 (PK0730/2026)
14 October 2026: Finance Minister Markus Marterbauer raised the 2027 deficit forecast from 3.5% to 3.6% and kept the 3% target for 2028 (trend/APA)

title: Temporarily stop family reunification for refugees
description: The government programme provided for a temporary suspension of family reunification for recognised refugees and holders of subsidiary protection, justified by the strain on schools and other public systems.
reasoning: Parliament created the legal basis in April 2025 and the Main Committee approved the government regulation, presented by Stocker, on 1 July 2025, suspending the processing of reunification applications for six months; it was extended for another six months in December 2025. In 2026 the implementation of the EU asylum and migration pact replaced the suspension with a quota system for family reunification.
key_evidence: 25 April 2025: National Council adopted the amendment to the Asylum Act 2005 allowing a temporary suspension (BGBl. I Nr. 17/2025)
1 July 2025: Main Committee approved the regulation (44/HA) presented by Chancellor Stocker; ÖVP, SPÖ, NEOS and FPÖ in favour, Greens against (PK0633/2025)
17 December 2025: suspension extended for six months (PK1207/2025)
20 May 2026: Asylum and Migration Pact Adaptation Act introduced a quota for family reunification (BGBl. I Nr. 39/2026; PK0730/2026)

title: Ban headscarves for girls under 14 at school
description: The coalition pledged a ban on girls up to the age of 14 wearing a headscarf at school, presented as protection of girls' self-determination.
reasoning: The National Council adopted the school-law amendment on 11 December 2025 with the votes of ÖVP, SPÖ, NEOS and FPÖ, and the ban applies from the 2026/27 school year, after an information phase from February 2026. The Greens voted against and consider the law unconstitutional; no Constitutional Court ruling on it was found as of October 2026.
key_evidence: 11 December 2025: National Council adopted the ban for pupils up to their 14th birthday in public and private schools; sanctions range from a clarifying talk to fines of €150–800 (PK1172/2025)
Promulgated as BGBl. I Nr. 117/2025 on 30 December 2025
In force from the start of the 2026/27 school year (PK0796/2026)

title: Allow the surveillance of encrypted messenger communication of suspected extremists
description: The programme pledged a constitutionally compliant power for the state-protection service to monitor messenger services ("Gefährderüberwachung") to prevent terrorist attacks.
reasoning: The cabinet adopted the bill on 18 June 2025 and the National Council passed it on 9 July 2025 by 105 votes to 71, with the FPÖ, the Greens and two NEOS MPs against; it was promulgated in September 2025. The Greens announced they would examine a challenge before the Constitutional Court.
key_evidence: 18 June 2025: cabinet decision on the 'constitutionally compliant introduction' of the surveillance of suspected extremists (BKA)
9 July 2025: National Council approval, 105 to 71 (PK0661/2025)
BGBl. I Nr. 54/2025 amending the State Protection and Intelligence Service Act and other laws

title: Rent brake: freeze regulated rents in 2025 and cap increases afterwards
description: The coalition pledged to freeze inflation-linked increases of regulated rents (old buildings, municipal and cooperative housing) in 2025, cap them at 1% in 2026 and 2% in 2027, and then limit indexation for all rents, including the free market.
reasoning: The 2025 freeze was adopted unanimously on 7 March 2025, days after the government took office. The 5th Rent Inflation Mitigation Act of December 2025 capped regulated rents at 1% (2026) and 2% (2027), limited indexation on the whole rental market above 3% inflation to half of the excess and extended minimum fixed-term leases from three to five years.
key_evidence: 7 March 2025: 4th Rent Inflation Mitigation Act suspended the 2025 indexation of regulated rents (PK0120/2025; BGBl. I Nr. 12/2025)
11 December 2025: 5th Rent Inflation Mitigation Act adopted with ÖVP, SPÖ, NEOS and Greens, FPÖ against (PK1171/2025; BGBl. I Nr. 114/2025)
Minimum term for fixed-term leases raised from three to five years for contracts from 1 January 2026, except small private landlords (BKA review)

title: Raise the early 'corridor' pension age to 63 and introduce a partial pension
description: The programme pledged to raise the minimum age for the early corridor pension (Korridorpension) from 62 to 63 and the required insurance years from 40 to 42, to introduce a partial pension (Teilpension) and a sustainability mechanism for the pension system.
reasoning: The stricter access to the corridor pension was enacted with the 2025 budget accompanying act, rising in quarterly steps of two months, and the partial pension was adopted in July 2025 and applies from 2026. The cabinet also adopted the sustainability mechanism in its pension package of 18 June 2025.
key_evidence: Budget Accompanying Act 2025 (BGBl. I Nr. 25/2025, adopted 16 June 2025): corridor pension age to 63, insurance years to 42
Partial pension adopted in the 2024/25 session, available from 2026 (PK0696/2025)
18 June 2025: cabinet adopted the pension package with partial pension and sustainability mechanism (BKA)

title: Reform social assistance with reduced benefits during a mandatory integration phase
description: The coalition pledged a reform of social assistance (Sozialhilfe NEU) linked to a mandatory integration programme, under which newcomers who have not yet paid into the system receive lower benefits during an integration phase. Stocker has called it one of the government's largest reform projects of the legislative period.
reasoning: The mandatory integration programme was launched in 2025, but as of October 2026 the social-assistance law itself had not been sent to public consultation. After a government working meeting on 17 October 2026 Stocker said the reform was 'on the home straight' and that talks with the federal states would precede the draft.
key_evidence: BKA review of 2025: 'Startschuss' for a mandatory integration programme with sanctions for refusal
17 October 2026: Stocker said lower social assistance would apply during the integration phase and that the draft would go to consultation 'as soon as possible' after talks with the Länder (BKA)

title: Cut non-wage labour costs
description: Reducing non-wage labour costs (Lohnnebenkosten) for employers was one of the coalition's economic goals, to be implemented when the budget allowed.
reasoning: The cut was agreed in the government's budget talks in spring 2026 and enacted with the Budget Accompanying Act 2027–2028 in July 2026: employers' contributions to the family burden equalisation fund (FLAF) fall by one percentage point from 2028. Because it only takes effect in 2028, the pledge is legislated but not yet delivered; Lower Austria's governor Johanna Mikl-Leitner (ÖVP) has asked for it to start in 2027.
key_evidence: 8 July 2026: National Council adopted the Budget Accompanying Act 2027–2028, which lowers non-wage labour costs from 2028 through lower FLAF contributions (PK0706/2026; BGBl. I Nr. 62/2026)
profil (9 May 2026): the government had fixed the cut the previous week
September 2026: Mikl-Leitner called for the cut to apply from 2027 rather than 2028 (Salzburg24/APA)

title: Create an independent federal public prosecutor's office (Bundesstaatsanwaltschaft)
description: ÖVP, SPÖ and NEOS agreed in their programme to replace the Justice Minister as the top authority giving instructions to prosecutors with an independent federal prosecutor's office, in order to depoliticise the chain of instructions.
reasoning: The government presented a draft on 29 June 2026 (a three-member collegial leadership within the Procurator General's office, six-year terms, selection by an expert commission with parliamentary approval) and held a public consultation from 30 June to 31 August 2026. Most submissions were critical, and the law needs a two-thirds majority, so the support of the FPÖ or the Greens; no parliamentary vote had taken place as of October 2026.
key_evidence: 29 June 2026: Justice Minister Anna Sporrer presented the agreed draft; ORF notes the project was in the government programme
Consultation 30 June – 31 August 2026 (oesterreich.gv.at)
August 2026: the Innsbruck Higher Regional Court, the judges' and prosecutors' associations and university experts criticised the draft (ORF)

title: Tighten the gun law after the Graz school shooting
description: After the shooting at a Graz secondary school on 10 June 2025, in which ten people were killed, Stocker's cabinet adopted a package on 18 June 2025 that included a tightening of the weapons law, which Stocker said would focus on prevention 'without calling responsible private gun ownership into question'.
reasoning: The National Council adopted the amendment to the Weapons Act on 24 September 2025 and it was promulgated in October 2025. It raised the minimum age for category B firearms (such as pistols) from 21 to 25 and for category C firearms from 18 to 21, lengthened the cooling-off period and strengthened psychological checks and data exchange between authorities.
key_evidence: 18 June 2025: cabinet package after the Graz shooting, including a €20 million compensation fund and stricter gun rules (BKA)
BGBl. I Nr. 56/2025 amending the Weapons Act 1996 (National Council 24 September 2025, Federal Council 9 October 2025)
Minimum ages raised from 21 to 25 (category B) and from 18 to 21 (category C) (PK0730/2026)

title: Reform and lengthen basic military service from 1 January 2027
description: On 27 July 2026 the cabinet chaired by Stocker adopted a military-service reform: basic service extended by three months of compulsory exercises (from six to nine months), pay raised to €1,000 a month, voluntary two-month extension of civilian service from 2027 and an automatic compulsory extension if conscript numbers fall too low. Stocker said the aim was for the reform to enter into force on 1 January 2027.
reasoning: The reform was agreed within the coalition and adopted by the cabinet, but it needs a two-thirds majority in Parliament, which the government said it would seek from the opposition. On 18 October 2026 Defence Minister Klaudia Tanner said the reform, including the timing of the civilian-service extension, was still being negotiated with the opposition; no parliamentary adoption had been reported as of October 2026.
key_evidence: 27 July 2026: cabinet decision at the Schwarzenberg barracks in Salzburg, based on the 'Stufenmodell' of the military-service commission (BKA)
Goal of entry into force on 1 January 2027; two-thirds majority required (BKA)
ORF, 27 July 2026: coalition agreement on the reform
18 October 2026: Tanner expected a cross-party agreement with the Greens or the FPÖ but said the details were still under negotiation (trend/APA)

title: Tax-free 'Zukunftsdepot' investment account for children
description: Stocker's own initiative, presented in late summer 2026: parents and relatives could invest up to €5,000 a year per child in a deposit free of capital-gains tax and account fees until the child turns 18, with a state start bonus of €500; the ÖVP had hoped for a start on 1 January 2027.
reasoning: After a dispute with the SPÖ-led Finance Ministry over financing and the start date, the coalition agreed on 17 October 2026 that the deposit will start on 1 July 2027, with the €500 bonus for children born from 1 January 2027. The enabling law had not yet been passed as of October 2026, and the start is six months later than the ÖVP had planned.
key_evidence: 6 September 2026: the Finance Ministry said a start on 1 January 2027 was 'technically practically impossible' and financing was missing (Salzburg24/APA)
17 October 2026: Stocker announced the agreement: start on 1 July 2027, €500 bonus for children born from 1 January 2027, up to €5,000 a year (BKA)
18 October 2026: both coalition partners said the budgetary cover was secured; the bonus is financed from the FLAF (news.at/APA)
